Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for taking the call last week. ResellCo is pulling together a few private-offer pilots and we need to validate how a reseller uplift would actually flow through a Redwood private offer across regions (US primary, some EMEA accounts later). A couple of concrete asks: 

- Can Redwood support a reseller-specific uplift (3–7%) layered on top of the private-offer unit price so the reseller can retain margin vs. list price?
- Which SKUs are eligible for uplift in marketplace private offers; do we need an explicit SKU mapping file?
- What happens to uplift if the customer misses commit thresholds (clawback or retroactive true-up)?

I attached a rough outline of the commit scenarios ResellCo is modeling (reseller_commit_outline.xlsx).

We'd like to align before we put a formal PO on the table — is there time for a 30m call next week? Copying AWS partner team to keep marketplace constraints on the thread.

Best,
Liam

Proposed times for a 30m sync: Wednesday 4/6 10:00 or Thursday 4/7 14:00 PT. Which works for you?

Liam / Naomi —

Digging into this with our ops playbook attached (uplift_playbook_v1.pdf) and a worked example (commit_scenarios.xlsx). High-level options we recommend: 

1) Uplift-as-passback (preferred): Redwood lists private-offer net price to customer. Reseller receives an automated passback equal to the uplift percent on usage invoiced through the private offer. Pros: clean accounting for customer, reseller gets predictable uplift. Cons: requires reseller payment routing setup in marketplace (works in AWS/GCP with partner routing).

2) Uplift-as-invoice-line: Redwood includes a secondary invoice line that invoices the uplift directly to the reseller or passes it through the customer invoice. Pros: simpler where passback is not supported. Cons: can complicate revenue recognition and tax handling.

Clawback/true-up recommendations: 
- Include a quarterly reconciliation clause with a 30–60 day true-up window; if commit targets are missed, revert uplift for the shortfall months and issue an offset on next invoice.
- For larger pilots, add a 90-day clawback holdback in escrow to be released after the first true-up.

Things I need from ResellCo to finalize ops: 
- SKU mapping (use Naomi's template)
- Target uplift percent per SKU or bundle (we can model tiered uplift too)
- Expected commit cadence and how you want early termination handled

I'm happy to walk through the commit_scenarios workbook on the call. Proposed: Thu 4/7 14:00 PT — same as Naomi's suggestion.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Channel Operations

Attachments: uplift_playbook_v1.pdf, commit_scenarios.xlsx

Liam —

Great sync today. To capture outcomes and next actions: 

Summary of agreed approach:
- Structure: Uplift-as-passback routed to ResellCo via AWS partner routing for the pilot (US). Redwood will record uplift as a passback liability and route settlement monthly.
- Escrow: Redwood to hold a 90-day holdback in our internal escrow account for the first quarter; if quarterly true-up shows commits met, Redwood will release the holdback. Jordan to draft the contract clause.
- SKUs: ResellCo to provide SKU mapping using our template; Redwood will validate eligibility and return a final SKU list within 3 business days.
- Clawback mechanics: Quarterly reconciliation, 30–60 day true-up window, shortfalls applied as offset to next settlement.

Action items and owners: 
- ResellCo (Liam): Upload final SKU mapping and sign the PO. Target: 2028-04-14.
- Redwood (Ben): Validate SKU eligibility and run final uplift passback simulation. Deliverable: commit_scenarios final workbook by 2028-04-12.
- Redwood (Jordan): Draft contract addendum including escrow and clawback language; circulate by 2028-04-11.

Links and artifacts: DocuSign link for PO (https://www.docusign.com/MLG-78910), HubSpot deal HS-123456, shared folder with simulation outputs (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c).

If anything above is incorrect, flag in reply-all. Otherwise we'll treat this as the baseline for drafting the private-offer and contract addendum.

Thanks everyone —
